newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toshiba delays U.S. launch of DVD players.
newsitem.headline: Toshiba delays U.S. launch of DVD players.

text.p: Toshiba Corp said on Tuesday it would delay the U.S. launch of its new high-capacity digital video disc (DVD) players until January or February because of a lack of software titles.

"A large number of DVD software titles won't be available until late January or early February," a Toshiba spokesman said. "The decision is in line with our policy of selling hardware and software at the same time."
Toshiba and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co started selling DVD players in Japan on November 1. Both said at the time they would start selling them later in the year in the United States.
A Matsushita spokesman said the company had not changed its plans.
The DVD format is expected to eventually replace video movies, compact discs (CDs) and CD-ROMs. A DVD looks like a CD, but can hold seven to 14 times as much data.

A group of the world's top 10 electronics and film makers that developed the DVD had planned to start selling the players in late summer in Japan. But tangled negotiations with Hollywood studios on copyright protection delayed the launch.
Toshiba said about 40 to 50 software titles will be available when its players hit the U.S. market. This will include at least two major hit films by Time Warner Inc, the spokesman said.
